lessons.title: Local Git Foundations
lessons.assistance_level: Full walkthrough for the guided cycle; limited assistance on the comparable challenge
lessons.note: Jeremy verified Git and the existing Node, npm, and Python tools; created a disposable local-only repository; inspected working, staged, and committed states; made three commits; restored an unwanted change; and completed a comparable NOTES.md Git cycle. He correctly explained staging, commits, local versus GitHub, M/AM status, .env versus .env.example, and a plain-text secret risk. Help on the challenge was limited to printf file-creation syntax. lessons.title: Local Branches, Merges, and Safe Recovery
lessons.assistance_level: Full walkthrough for guided branch, merge, and recovery; substantial guided help on the comparable challenge
lessons.note: Jeremy verified the prior clean three-commit local repository; created and compared guided and comparable branches; completed two fast-forward-only merges; preserved and reversed a deliberate bad commit with revert; corrected a README formatting defect found through diff inspection; and finished on clean main at b1bf13d with seven commits, no remote, and an ignored/untracked .env. Exact commands and verification scaffolding were supplied, and core concepts required repeated correction, so substantial assistance is recorded. Independent mastery was not claimed.

lessons.title: Git Identity, Privacy, and GitHub Readiness
lessons.assistance_level: Full walkthrough for the beginner identity/privacy model and failure analysis; guided help for the consequential identity and scope decisions
lessons.note: Jeremy verified the exact clean seven-commit practice repository and current identity sources; chose Jeremy Bernhardt plus his GitHub-provided noreply address as the global personal default; confirmed GitHub email-privacy settings; separately approved configuration; chose local overrides for a future employer identity; and verified the prospective identity without changing existing commits or adding a remote. His initial privacy/push explanation needed correction, and full-history failure and limitation analysis was supplied. Independent mastery was not claimed.

lessons.title: Private GitHub Course Repository and First Verified Push
lessons.assistance_level: Full walkthrough for repository, authentication, permission, credential, implementation, and verification models; Jeremy supplied specifications and approvals
lessons.note: Jeremy defined or approved the exact private repository specification, kept the disposable history separate, identified that a push would not prove content accuracy, and gave separate informed approval before creation, connection, and first push. AI installed and authenticated the verified official GitHub CLI, prepared and inspected the separate repository, performed the approved actions, and independently verified owner, privacy, branch, commit, tree, tracking, exclusions, and fresh-clone reconstruction. The planned Module 0 lesson sequence is complete with substantial assistance; independent mastery and resume-level proficiency are not claimed.

lessons.title: Defining Outcomes, Constraints, and Done Criteria
lessons.assistance_level: Full structured walkthrough for the guided work brief; limited targeted help on the different variance-report transfer

In a different variance-report scenario he independently identified materiality and an actual-versus-actual failure; one targeted revision was needed to recenter the outcome and provide an exact known-answer test.
